doc.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006

chapter: New Orleans families, lifestyle and retirement
title: Discouraging his kids from jazz and warning about the lifestyle
summary: He steered his kids to classical, warns students of drug temptations, and says the slow people make it.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How do I say this? Would the parents push the kids into music or was it just there all the time and the kids —

It was there all the time. I tried to discourage mine to tell the truth about it. ‘Cause I just wanted them, I really didn’t want them to play jazz. I was hoping that they wouldn’t and © Fillius Jazz Archive -28-

that’s why I was sending them to get all that classical technique and all that so they could play some different kinds of music, I said there’s enough jazz. ‘Cause jazz has — another thing, everybody’s not supposed to play jazz. The environment that they put them in, and I tell kids now I say man you better know what you’re doing when you want to play jazz. ‘Cause I’ve seen kids that come out of very good families and did this and you see them ten years later and they’re out on the streets with all kinds of habits, doing this and doing that and people look at me, I say, “maybe you’re not supposed to be in jazz, man, maybe you’re supposed to do something else.” ‘Cause the lifestyle sometimes it’ll be too much for them. And people look at me and say, “man why are you discouraging?” I say I’m not discouraging them but I’m letting them know what’s ahead because jazz, everybody’s not supposed to fool with that. And I know because I’ve been around people that did everything in the world and I tell them now whatever you do you can die right here on the stand, it ain’t going to effect me one bit. You can tell me whatever’s going to get you high and make you feel good. I had people tell me said man, the way you could play, with what all you’re doing, if you was doing some of them other things, if you had some of this and you had some of that, man you would be the baddest cat in the world. I said yeah, so I don’t want to be the baddest cat in the world. I want to be the baddest cat in the world in my right mind. Everything — I’m crazy enough now. I got to be in my right mind at all times. I don’t even drink, I can’t drink. I mean like they’d go to sip at the bar, anything that gets me out of my mind I mean I just can’t deal with it. And I tell people I say man y’all better know what you’re doing. It’s good and I tell parents, this is good, but you’ve got to kind of monitor this ‘cause when they get out from under your wings and even with the best of training, that outside crowd will take them out. You know, ‘cause they get with a hip crowd, just don’t be hip. Now I never was hip. That’s another thing. I never was a hip cat.

Yeah. Hip cats, I tell them, all the hip cats always fell by the wayside, you know. The slow people are the ones, you know, who make it. But the hip cats that’s cause it’s going to be hip for a little while and it’s all going to be gone. So it’s the slow people is the ones who will make it in the end.
